rationale: Jesus calls himself, or at least the figure whose presence rules out fasting, "the bridegroom" (40.9.15, BSB). In Hosea 2 God speaks as Israel's husband: "you will call Me 'my Husband,'" and "I will betroth you to Me forever" (28.2.16, 28.2.19, BSB). The Pulpit Commentary reports that a scholar it names only as Nosgen "sees in this a claim to be the expected Bridegroom of Israel," citing Hosea 2:19-20 with Jeremiah 3 and Ezekiel 16. Matthew names no prophet, uses no formula, and Hosea 2 never uses the word "bridegroom," so this is an allusion at most; the label is plausible because one named reader argues it, reported here only secondhand, and the verbal overlap is an image (God as husband) rather than shared words.
